submission.natural_language_explanation: Fires on runs of ALL-CAPS English text (headlines, section headings, names and case captions in capitals), peaking at 0.55-1.0 of max on capitalised function words and word pieces inside a multi-word caps run (' THROUGH'/'OUGH', ' THE', ' FOR', ' TO', ' ON', 'ING', 'ENT', 'ARD', the '-' in 'ANNE-MARIE'), from the second caps word onward; Title Case headlines reach only about 0.4-0.65 (e.g. 'Gobbles Up', 'Puts Us') and the same words in lowercase stay low. Floor: the first token of any prompt sits at about 0.20 of max, short plain lowercase sentences with concrete nouns and verbs peak at 0.20-0.25, but longer ordinary prose often reaches 0.25-0.35 on pronouns, auxiliaries and 'that'/'to' (weakly active), so a negative must be short plain prose, code, or lowercase text.
